summary: EU-WEST dedicated capacity: sustained latency spikes and request timeouts caused by noisy tenant GPU contention
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaChat on a Dedicated cluster in eu-west reported sustained end-to-end latency regression (p50 from ~80ms to 600-1200ms) and intermittent request timeouts (504) for production inference routes. The degradation started during a traffic spike on 2026-03-12 morning and persisted despite autoscaler activity.

Impact:
- Multiple production customer-facing endpoints experienced increased latency and ~3-7% of requests returned 504 over a 90-minute window.
- Affected ~4 apps belonging to NovaChat; business impact: degraded user experience and some failed chat sessions.
- Not a global outage; limited to the customer's dedicated pool in eu-west.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-03-12 08:14 UTC: NovaChat alerts to Support via portal; included sample request IDs and stack traces.
- 2026-03-12 08:20 UTC: Support triaged, escalated to SRE and Serving-Infra.
- 2026-03-12 08:35 UTC: Observability shows sustained GPU utilisation hotspots on 3 hosts, prolonged kernel scheduling delays, and elevated queue length in request-router.
- 2026-03-12 09:05 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: pinning affected routes to standby pool and increasing min replicas for NovaChat; partial improvement.
- 2026-03-12 10:10 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis updated after heap of traces: single tenant job producing very large continuous batches and a model variant triggering inefficient CUDA kernels causing slot contention.

Steps to reproduce (dev environment):
1) Deploy a dedicated pool with similar instance types and driver versions (NVIDIA 545.xx).
2) Send a steady stream of concurrent requests with artificially large prompt sizes to one tenant route emulating NovaChat peak traffic (200 concurrent requests, ~1.2k token prompts).
3) Observe serve-runtime metrics: kernel latency, queue length, and host-level GPU metrics.

Observed logs / snippets:
- router: "request-queue-time=512ms route=novachat-chat pool=eu-west-dedicated queue-length=46"
- serving-runtime: "kv-cache-lock-wait=120ms host=gw-eu-03 gid=0"
- node-exporter: "nvidia_gpu_utilization=98%, smi_pending_cmds=27, pcie_rx_errors=0"
- nginx: "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream"

Hypotheses considered:
- Noisy tenant: single customer workload producing oversized batches and long-running kernels blocking GPU scheduling.
- Mis-sized autoscaler: autoscaler configured with conservative scale-up window and low max burst capacity, causing reactive scaling lag.
- GPU driver/kernel mismatch on 3 hosts (gw-eu-01/02/03) leading to degraded kernel preemption behaviour.

Immediate actions taken:
- Support pinned NovaChat routes to a separate standby pool at 09:05 UTC to relieve contention (workaround).
- Increased min-replicas for NovaChat in Dedicated config to keep buffer capacity during spikes.
- Temporarily disabled cross-tenant packing on affected hosts.
- Added a short-term autoscaler override (faster scale-up) for the customer's pool.

Desired state / success criteria:
- Latencies return to baseline (p50 < 150ms) and request success rate > 99.7% for NovaChat routes.
- No recurring contention events across the dedicated fleet.

Notes on customer communication:
- Customer notified at 09:20 UTC of mitigation and advised of ongoing investigation.
- Follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-13 11:00 UTC with NovaChat account team to review permanent mitigations.
comments: 2026-03-12 08:22 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE and Serving-Infra. Customer provided request IDs: r-4637, r-4640, r-4652.

2026-03-12 08:41 - SRE (Daniel Kim): Observed 3 hosts with >95% GPU util and long kernel wait times. Queue length correlated with host hotspots. Spinning up investigation on driver versions and kernel preemption settings.
2026-03-12 09:07 - Support (Aisha Patel): Pinned routes to standby pool; customer reports partial recovery.

2026-03-12 09:25 - Serving-Infra (Lina Ortega): Found that one tenant session was consistently batching to 512 tokens with batch aggregation enabled. That behavior combined with an older 545.45 driver on gw-eu-03 increased kernel latency significantly.

2026-03-12 10:18 - Daniel Kim: Preliminary root cause points to noisy tenant + autoscaler slowness + occasional driver mismatch. Raising INT ticket to coordinate driver rollout and autoscale policy change: INT-409.
2026-03-12 11:02 - Customer (NovaChat - ops@novachat.com): Thanks for the quick mitigation, would like a permanent fix. Please share follow-up actions and ETA.
2026-03-13 09:05 - Daniel Kim: Preparing a post-incident plan; will propose driver upgrade schedule and QoS/enforcement rules to prevent a single tenant from saturating GPU resources.
investigation_notes: Metric correlation: high request-queue-time aligns with spikes in smi_pending_cmds and GPU SM utilization >95% on 3 hosts (gw-eu-01/02/03).

Serving runtime trace showed long-running kernel launches for specific op kernels in model 'mistral-7b-v2' when input sequence length >1k tokens; these runs block subsequent CUDA streams on same device.
Autoscaler logs show scale-up actions triggered at 08:38 UTC but new nodes became healthy only at ~08:55 UTC due to conservative readiness checks and slow instance boot times.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: pinned NovaChat routes to standby pool and increased min-replicas; result: throughput restored to acceptable levels, error rate fell to <0.3%.

Medium-term fixes planned before 2026-03-20: (1) driver upgrade to NVIDIA 555.xx across eu-west fleet to improve preemption, (2) autoscaler policy change to reduce scale-up cooldown and increase burst capacity, (3) implement per-tenant soft-QoS limits to cap maximum aggregate batch size/throughput.
A follow-up INT ticket (INT-409) opened to schedule the driver rollout and change autoscaler policy. Serving-Infra PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4382.
Action items assigned to infra and platform: Daniel Kim (infra) and Lina Ortega (serving-infra).
follow_up_tasks: INT-409: Schedule staged driver upgrade for eu-west hosts and validate preemption improvements (owner: Daniel Kim).
ENG-OPS-1721: Implement per-tenant batching guards and cross-tenant packing limits with throttling policy (owner: Lina Ortega).
OPS-245: Review and adjust autoscaler readiness checks and reduce scale-up window for dedicated pools (owner: Maya Singh).
Customer follow-up: 2026-03-13 11:00 UTC review call with NovaChat to confirm permanent mitigation plan (owner: Aisha Patel).
